land.text: the Hejaz, where Ibn al-Zubayr was proclaimed

predecessors.note: The Second Fitna page lists the 'Dissolution of the Zubayrid Caliphate' among the results of the war.

land.text: the Hejaz without Ta'if, the last Zubayrid land

successors.note: 'The Hejaz came under Umayyad control' in October 692.

capitals.name: Mecca
capitals.note: 'By September 683, he had taken control of Mecca'; the page has him based in Mecca until his death.

correction.text: 683: the Hejaz, Iraq, Egypt, Yemen and the Iran of the 674 shape outside Khorasan (Fars and Kerman among them)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Zubayrid row; it gives the Umayyads Arabia, Persia and Iraq in 682-691). The provinces that 'offered their allegiance, including Egypt, Kufa, Yemen', the Hejaz, and the Iranian dependencies of Basra and Kufa (Fars and Kerman by their coins; Jibal and Azerbaijan by the Mukhtar page; the rest my reading, confidence 1). Khorasan is Ibn Khazim's, drawn as a vassal outside the shape.

correction.text: 684: as 683 plus the Jazira (Zufar and the Qays)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Qays of northern Syria are crushed at Marj Rahit (August 684) and the survivors keep Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty in the Jazira.

correction.text: 685-686: the Hejaz, Yemen, the Basra region, the Iranian dependencies other than Fars, Kerman and Mukhtar's north-west, and the Jazira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Egypt goes in March 685, Fars and Kerman to the Azariqa in 685 and Kufa to Mukhtar in October 685 (Second Fitna and Abd Allah pages); what is left is the Hejaz, Yemen and Basra, where Mus'ab was the Zubayrid governor. The year takes the end-of-year state. Widened (review of 2026-10-19): Khuzestan, Isfahan, Sistan and the rest of Iran outside Fars, Kerman, Khorasan and Mukhtar's Jibal and Azerbaijan stay Zubayrid, and the Jazira (Qays) too.

correction.text: 687: the Hejaz, Iraq and Yemen, the Iranian dependencies except Fars and Kerman, and the Jazira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Mus'ab retakes Kufa on 3 April 687 (Mukhtar page), so Iraq is Zubayrid again; Yemen still is. Mukhtar's Jibal and Azerbaijan return with Kufa (confidence 1).

correction.text: 688: the Hejaz and Iraq with its Iranian dependencies and the Jazira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Najda 'captured Yemen and Hadhramawt in 688' (Second Fitna page); the Hejaz and Iraq remain.

correction.text: 689-690: the Hejaz without Ta'if, Iraq with its Iranian dependencies, and the Jazira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Najda 'occupied Ta'if in 689' (Second Fitna page), a small hole in the Hejaz; Iraq is held until Maskin in October 691.

New keyframe. Iraq falls to Abd al-Malik after Maskin (October 691); Mecca falls in October 692. The year 691 takes the end-of-year state. Iraq, its dependencies and the Jazira fall in October 691 (ledger); the year takes the end-of-year state.

region.text: Yemen, which offered allegiance

ledger.note: Page silent on the date. Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page: 'Most of the Islamic provinces offered their allegiance, including Egypt, Kufa, Yemen.' Placed with the proclamation (683) as the bridging year. Najda's Kharijites took Yemen from him in 688. Re-read on the Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page (2026-10-19): 'Most of the Islamic provinces offered their allegiance' after Yazid's death in November 683 and Mu'awiya II's death, with no date per province; Yemen is named, no year. 683 stays a bridging.

region.text: Fars and Kerman, where his coins were struck

ledger.note: Page silent on when. Second Fitna page: Ibn al-Zubayr's coins were struck 'as far east as Fars and Kirman', and the Azariqa 'captured Fars and Kirman from the Zubayrids in 685'; neither sentence dates the Zubayrid hold, so 683 (the proclamation) is bridging. The Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page has a Fars dirham of 690/91, after the Azariqa had taken the country, which suggests the hold was nominal or partial. Re-read (2026-10-19): the Abd Allah page says only that coins were minted in his name 'as far as Kerman and Fars, both dependencies of Basra', with a Fars dirham of 690/91 in the caption; no date for either joining.

region.text: northern Syria, where the Qaysi tribes backed him

ledger.note: Page silent on the date. Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page: 'Qaysi tribes of northern Syria' backed him while 'central and southern Syria remained loyal to the Umayyads'. Placed with the proclamation. Syria was never his: the zone is the Qays country contested with Marwan, and 'northern' is read as Aleppo, Idlib and Raqqa. Re-read (2026-10-19): the Abd Allah page dates Marj Rahit to July 684 and has the Qays fleeing to the Jazira; nothing dates the Qays' support before it.

region.text: the Hejaz, with Mecca as seat of the counter-caliph

ledger.note: Nov 683: Ibn al-Zubayr proclaims himself caliph at Mecca. Page: 'before proclaiming himself caliph in the wake of Yazid's death in 683'; 'By September 683, he had taken control of Mecca'; the page's succession box reads 'Caliph November 683 - November 692'. He wanted 'to re-establish the Hejaz as the political center of the Caliphate'; the Hejaz stayed under his control until his death in 692.

region.text: Iraq (Kufa and Basra) and Egypt, which recognised him

ledger.note: Nov 683 on: Second Fitna page: Ibn al-Zubayr 'was openly proclaimed caliph' after Yazid's death in November 683; 'Iraq and Egypt recognized him soon after, and most provinces recognized Ibn al-Zubayr as caliph'. 'Soon after' gives no month, so the date is the proclamation's.

region.text: the Iranian dependencies of Basra and Kufa other than Fars and Kerman: Jibal, Azerbaijan, Khuzestan, Isfahan, Sistan and the rest of the Iran of the 674 shape outside Khorasan

ledger.note: Page silent on a date and on the list: the Mukhtar page has Iraq, once Mukhtar took Kufa from the Zubayrid governor, with 'its dependencies including Arminiya, Adharbayjan, Jibal and parts of the Jazira'; the Second Fitna page 'most provinces recognized Ibn al-Zubayr'. Jibal and Azerbaijan are the page's words; Khuzestan, Isfahan, Sistan and the rest are my reading of 'dependencies of Iraq' (review of 2026-10-19: without them central Iran had no holder in 683-691). Arminiya is not drawn: the Arab-Byzantine wars page has the Muslims conquering almost all of Armenia in 692. Mirror of umayyad /ledger/13.

region.text: Khorasan with the Afghan lands of the 674 shape, held by Abd Allah ibn Khazim

ledger.note: 684: Salm appointed Ibn Khazim in the summer of 684 (Second Fitna page); he 'gave his allegiance to the Mecca-based caliph Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr' and was the 'nominal Zubayrid governor of the same province between 684 and his death' (Ibn Khazim page, 2026-10-19), without a year for the recognition and without tribute. Region widened with the umayyad-caliphate loss of 684.

region.text: northern Syria

ledger.note: Aug 684: Marj Rahit. Page: Marwan 'was acknowledged as caliph at Jabiya in June 684' and at Marj Rahit in August 684 'pro-Zubayrid Qays, under Dahhak, were crushed by Marwan's pro-Umayyad forces'. The page does not locate the Qays districts, so the zone follows the Abd Allah page's 'northern Syria'.

region.text: the Jazira, where the Qaysi survivors of Marj Rahit kept Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty

ledger.note: Aug 684: after Marj Rahit 'The surviving Qaysis fled to the Jazira under Zufar ibn al-Harith al-Kilabi, who continued to recognize Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty'. The page gives no extent and no governor; the Second Fitna page has Abd al-Malik besieging the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya in 691.

region.text: Fars and Kerman, taken by the Azariqa Kharijites

ledger.note: Second Fitna page: the Azariqa 'captured Fars and Kirman from the Zubayrids in 685'. The Azariqa page dates their move to Fars to after the Battle of Sillabra in May 686, which would put it in 686; the Second Fitna year is used. Both pages say the Azariqa held these lands for years.

region.text: Egypt, taken by Marwan and his son Abd al-Aziz

ledger.note: Mar 685: Egypt lost. Page: 'in March 685, Ibn al-Zubayr lost the economically important province of Egypt to Marwan'. The Second Fitna page has Marwan and his son Abd al-Aziz 'expelled the Zubayrid governor of Egypt' during Marwan's caliphate (June 684 to April 685); the Maghreb page 'late 684'. March 685 is used.

region.text: Kufa and most of Iraq (Basra stayed Zubayrid), taken by Mukhtar

ledger.note: Oct 685: Second Fitna page: Mukhtar 'overthrew the Zubayrid governor and seized Kufa' in October 685 and held 'most of Iraq and parts of north-western Iran'. The Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page: Mukhtar's partisans 'drove out the Zubayrid authorities from Kufa in October 685'. Basra is left out because Mus'ab, who killed Mukhtar, was the Zubayrid governor of Basra (Second Fitna page).

region.text: north-western Iran: the Jibal and Azerbaijan

ledger.note: Page silent on when: after taking Kufa Mukhtar 'controlled most of Iraq and its dependencies including Arminiya, Adharbayjan, Jibal and parts of the Jazira' (placed after Ayn al-Warda, January 685, and before Mosul, July 686; the Second Fitna page 'parts of north-western Iran'). Placed with Kufa (October 685). Mirror of mukhtarid /ledger/0; Arminiya and the Jazira are not drawn.

region.text: Kufa and Iraq (Basra stayed Zubayrid), and the Jibal and Azerbaijan, retaken by Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr

ledger.note: 3 Apr 687: Mukhtar page: Mus'ab 'besieged Mukhtar's palace for four months' and 'on 3 April 687 Mukhtar came out of the palace with nineteen supporters' and was killed. The page gives Kufa; that the rest of Mukhtar's Iraq returned with it is my reading. The Abd Allah page: Mus'ab 'reasserted Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty [in Iraq] by 687'. Widened (review of 2026-10-19) with Mukhtar's north-western Iran, which is his dossier's loss of the same day; the Mukhtar page does not say who held the Jibal and Azerbaijan afterwards (Mus'ab, 'launched an assault against Kufa' in 687, took the palace), so that part is confidence 1.

region.text: Yemen and Hadhramawt, taken by Najda

ledger.note: Second Fitna page: Najda 'captured Yemen and Hadhramawt in 688'. The Najdat page puts the invasion of Yemen in 687, the Abd Allah page c.687/688; the Second Fitna year is used.

region.text: Ta'if, occupied by the Najdat

ledger.note: Second Fitna page: Najda 'occupied Ta'if in 689'; the Abd Allah page agrees ('Ta'if in 689'). The Najdat page, opened for the Najdat dossier, does not mention Ta'if and says the Najdat did not attack the holy villages.

region.text: Iraq, conquered by Abd al-Malik after Maskin, with its dependencies in Iran (Fars and Kerman are the Azariqa's)

ledger.note: Oct 691: Second Fitna page: Mus'ab 'was killed at the Battle of Maskin in October 691' and 'Abd al-Malik reconquered Iraq after the Battle of Maskin'; the Abd Allah page: 'his forces conquered Iraq and killed Mus'ab'. Widened (review of 2026-10-19) to mirror umayyad /ledger/20: 'Abd al-Malik then secured Iraq and most of its dependencies' (Second Fitna page).

region.text: the Jazira, where Abd al-Malik besieged the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya

ledger.note: 691: 'In 691, he besieged the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya in the Jazira'; the page does not say when it fell, so 691 is my bridging for the Jazira's return, with Iraq. Mirror of the umayyad-caliphate gain of the Jazira in October 691.

region.text: Khorasan with the Afghan lands of the 674 shape

ledger.note: 692: 'At some time before the end of 692, Ibn Khazim was intercepted and killed by Bukayr ibn Wisha al-Sa'di's troops' (Ibn Khazim page, 2026-10-19); Bukayr, who sent his head to Abd al-Malik, succeeded him. The Second Fitna page has 691. Moved from 691 and raised from confidence 1; mirror of umayyad /ledger/19.

region.text: Mecca, besieged by al-Hajjaj

ledger.note: Mar 692: Second Fitna page: the siege of Mecca by al-Hajjaj began in March 692; the Abd Allah page: 'Al-Hajjaj besieged Mecca for six months'. The earlier siege by Husayn ibn Numayr (from 24 September 683) came before Ibn al-Zubayr was proclaimed and is not an event of this state.

region.text: Mecca and the Hejaz

ledger.note: Oct 692: Mecca falls. Second Fitna page: Ibn al-Zubayr 'was killed in October/November 692, and the Hejaz came under Umayyad control'.

region.text: the Hejaz without Ta'if: Mecca and Medina

ledger.note: Oct 692: 'the Hejaz came under Umayyad control' after Ibn al-Zubayr's death (Second Fitna page; the Abd Allah page 'ultimately defeated and killed in 692'). Ta'if (Najdat since 689) is not part of the loss; it goes to the Umayyads with the Najdat lands in 693.

region.text: the Hejaz without Ta'if, his last territory

ledger.note: Oct 692: death of Ibn al-Zubayr. The Second Fitna page lists the 'Dissolution of the Zubayrid Caliphate' as a result and dates his death October/November 692.

wars.name: Second Fitna

zones.text: the Hejaz, the siege of Mecca in 683 and 692

wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: Ibn al-Zubayr killed in October/November 692, the Zubayrid Caliphate dissolved.
wars.note: The page's infobox dates the war 680-692. Harra (summer 683), Marj Rahit (August 684), Khazir (August 686) and Maskin (October 691) are the main battles.

certainty.note: Authority outside the Hejaz was 'largely nominal' (Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page); the allegiance of provinces is recorded, not their borders.

notes:
Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19 from three pages. State Cliopatria lacks. Not on the pages: where Syria's Qays sat before Marj Rahit, the month of the allegiance of Iraq, Egypt and Yemen, the date Khorasan returned to Umayyad rule, and whether Medina was Zubayrid between the Harra (summer 683) and the end of the Umayyad army's stay (the Abd Allah page says only that the Hejaz stayed under his control to 692). The Fars dirham of 690/91 (Abd Allah page) sits oddly with the Azariqa hold of Fars from 685 (Second Fitna page): either the hold was partial or the coins were nominal. Counterparts without dossiers: Abd Allah ibn Khazim (a person). The Umayyad dossier of this group has the matching gains of Egypt (685), northern Syria (684), Iraq (691), Khorasan (691) and the Hejaz (692).
Repair of 2026-10-19 (review me-07): Iran outside Fars, Kerman and Khorasan, which the Umayyad 684-691 keyframe dropped, is now Zubayrid from 683 (the Jibal and Azerbaijan by the Mukhtar page, the rest at confidence 1), with the loss of the Jibal and Azerbaijan to Mukhtar in October 685 and their return in April 687, and Iraq with all these dependencies lost to Abd al-Malik in October 691. The Jazira (Qays under Zufar) is Zubayrid from August 684 to 691 (Abd Allah page; Second Fitna page). Khorasan's vassal pair now covers the Afghan lands of the 674 shape and ends in 692 (Ibn Khazim page; the Second Fitna page says 691). The Hejaz handed to the Umayyads in 692 excludes Ta'if. Arminiya is not drawn (see umayyad-caliphate). Thin items re-read: no page dates the joining of Yemen, Fars and Kerman or the Qays' support; they stay at confidence 1.
